Question 13(b) [4 marks]: Outline how supply chain management can be used to improve performance objectives in operations.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
3–4 marks: Sketches in general terms how supply chain management can be used to improve performance objectives in operations
2 marks: Sketches in general terms how supply chain management can be used to improve a performance objective in operations
1 marks: Identifies how supply chain management can be used to improve performance objectives in operations

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Supply chain management is an operations strategy to increase operations performance by making changes to the way inputs, partly completed goods and finished goods are obtained, transported, warehoused and delivered to customers. It can improve the performance objectives of speed and cost. Speed can be improved by securing better, more reliable transport and logistics, either owned by the company (better trucks) or outsourced to third parties with best practices (DHL). Cost can be improved by better negotiations with suppliers, for example securing volume discounts from a smaller number of suppliers by rationalising the supply chain.
